variant_reviews.comparison: Condition on the entire observed vector (X1,...,XT), using its generated sub-sigma-algebra. E-star of an integrable bootstrap quantity is condExp with respect to that sigma-algebra; Prob-star of an event is the conditional expectation of its indicator, or the event mass under a regular conditional bootstrap kernel. It is not conditioning on an equality event with positive probability assumed, and not merely conditioning on a fitted statistic. The conditional value is a random function of the observed data; the bootstrap randomness is integrated out. On the finite probability space setting the trimmed measure is finite, but measurability and integrability still need to be satisfied rather than using condExp’s zero fallback. Conditional kernels identify versions only almost everywhere under the data law, not at every imaginable sample vector.

variant_reviews.comparison: For the given positive bandwidth k_T form C[j1,j2]=K((j1-j2)/k_T) on indices 1,...,T and use the centered Gaussian law with covariance C. K(0)=1 makes each marginal variance one; the vector is generally correlated, not T independent standard Gaussians. Nonnegative entries and symmetry alone do not imply PSD: the source’s nonnegative integrable Fourier transform provides the missing quadratic-form argument. Singular PSD covariance is allowed; positive definiteness is not required. multivariateGaussian maps a non-PSD input to a degenerate fallback, so checking PSD is essential to assert the prescribed covariance. To realize the bootstrap, generate fresh multiplier randomness with this law conditional on the observed data, independent of observations for fixed tuning parameters, rather than treating the source data as the Gaussian multipliers themselves.
